{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My ex-husband, who I blamed for everything, wrote a letter to the custody mediator supporting my parenting abilities. My own mother, who I trusted completely, had been telling the mediator I was unstable. The man I'd demonized defended me while my mother tried to take my children.

CANDIDATE A:
The ruthless competitor who'd been trying to acquire my company warned me about a critical regulatory change that would affect my main product. Meanwhile, my trusted corporate lawyer—who I later learned was also representing that same competitor—had been slow-walking my compliance filings. The rival I feared saved me while my own counsel was sabotaging me.

CANDIDATE B:
During the custody dispute, my ex-husband fought for maximum time while my mother supported me, testifying to my parenting abilities and providing childcare. Both behaved as their relationships to me would predict.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:50"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories involve a betrayal by a trusted figure and an unexpected ally from an adversarial position, highlighting the reversal of expected support and opposition."}
